solutions.check: bars rebuilt from the blog's numbered answers (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Corporation displaying striking power, restricting one

indicators.note: to restrict something is to hem it in, so the first word's letters close around the second

blocks.note: the force of a blow, as a boxer's power to strike
one = A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A big company showing off its muscle while keeping one person in check.
explanation.walkthrough: PUNCH closes round A to make PAUNCH. 'Corporation' looks like a business, but in older slang it means a big belly.
explanation.definitionFit: Corporation is an old jocular word for a large belly, which is what a paunch is.

clue.text: Sweet cake down under? It has fat, a spoonful, mixed in it

indicators.note: mixed means stirred together, so these letters are combined in a new order

blocks.note: the twelve letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: An Australian sweet cake recipe calling for fat and a spoonful of something stirred in.
explanation.walkthrough: The recipe reading makes 'fat' and 'spoonful' look like ingredients; they are the letters of the answer. 'Down under' means Australia.
explanation.definitionFit: Puftaloonas are Australian fried scones or cakes, usually eaten hot with jam, honey or golden syrup.

clue.text: Volume welcomed by a sign of disapproval from the start (5, two words)

indicators.note: a guest welcomed by hosts is taken in among them, so one piece goes inside the other

blocks.note: taken as written
a boo is a jeer of disapproval; the volume letter goes inside it
V is the abbreviation for volume

explanation.surface: A book met with jeers right from the beginning.
explanation.walkthrough: A plus BOO with V inside gives AB OVO.
explanation.definitionFit: Ab ovo is Latin for 'from the egg', meaning from the very beginning.

clue.text: Crowns once placed on sovereign's head? This shows admiration (6, two words)

indicators.note: in a down entry, placed on means set above, so the heads come first
the head of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: noll or nole is an obsolete word for the head or crown
the first letter of sovereign

explanation.surface: Crowns that were once set on a monarch's head, a sight worthy of admiration.
explanation.walkthrough: NOLES above S gives NO LESS. 'Crowns' suggests regalia but means heads, and 'once' flags the obsolete word.
explanation.definitionFit: Said after naming something impressive, 'no less' is an exclamation expressing surprise or admiration.

clue.text: Old gull making good after losing fish?

indicators.note: losing something means it is taken away, so the fish letters are removed

blocks.note: cobbling means mending or repairing, as a cobbler does with shoes
the ling is a long fish of the cod family; these letters go

explanation.surface: An old fool who comes good after losing a fish.
explanation.walkthrough: COBBLING without LING gives COBB. 'Gull' looks like a dupe, but it is the seabird.
explanation.definitionFit: Cob or cobb is an old name for a gull, especially the great black-backed gull.

clue.text: Rap hand delivered roughly – it's low-level stuff

indicators.note: something delivered roughly is knocked about in transit, so the letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A rap performance given clumsily is dismissed as base stuff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Low-level' sounds like a put-down of the rap, but is literal: the layer lies deep in the soil.
explanation.definitionFit: Hardpan is a hardened, impervious layer of soil lying beneath the topsoil, so it is material at a low level.

clue.text: One with morbid aversion dodging pibroch heartlessly

indicators.note: without a heart means the central letter of the word is removed
dodging suggests darting about, so the remaining letters move into a new order

blocks.note: pibroch, bagpipe music, loses its middle letter R

explanation.surface: Someone who hates bagpipes ducking out of a pibroch performance without enthusiasm.
explanation.walkthrough: A pibroch is a piece of classical Highland bagpipe music; its central R goes, and the six letters left are rearranged into PHOBIC.
explanation.definitionFit: A phobic is a noun for a person who suffers from a phobia, an irrational, morbid fear or aversion.

clue.text: Scotch burn, one entering part of garden?

indicators.note: entering something means going inside it, so the single letter goes into the garden word

blocks.note: a plot is a patch of garden ground
one = A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Is a Scottish stream one that runs into part of the garden?
explanation.walkthrough: A goes into PLOT to make PLOAT. 'Burn' suggests a Scottish stream but is the verb, to scald.
explanation.definitionFit: Ploat is a Scots verb meaning to scald or plunge into boiling water, so a Scottish word for burn.

clue.text: Eccentric offspring? Favourite may well be this

blocks.note: first reading: a strange male child, split into two short words
second meaning: describing a betting favourite whose chance is better than even

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags the first meaning as a playful split of the word into two.
explanation.definitionFit: In betting, a favourite priced at less than evens is described as odds-on, while an odd son is a peculiar child.

clue.text: Troubled sahib, male not well inside, by God

indicators.note: troubled means disturbed, so the letters are rearranged
inside places the male and unwell pieces within the rearranged letters

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged; they are split to take the rest
M is the abbreviation for male
unwell, ill

explanation.surface: A worried Raj gentleman who is feeling poorly swears by God.
explanation.walkthrough: A sahib was the title given to a European man in colonial India. 'By God' reads as the sahib's oath but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Bismillah is the Arabic invocation 'in the name of God', an exclamation used much as 'by God' is.

clue.text: How decimals are calculated, requiring energy with concentration?

blocks.note: the decimal system counts in tens
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: Working out decimals takes effort and close concentration.
explanation.walkthrough: IN TENS plus E gives INTENSE.
explanation.definitionFit: Intense describes great focus or earnestness, so something done intensely is done with concentration.

clue.text: It transfers motion, number inside shifting touch faster

indicators.note: inside puts the single letter within the rearranged letters
shifting means moving about, so the letters change places

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged, split to hold the number
N is the abbreviation for number

explanation.surface: A device that passes on movement, a figure inside making contact more quickly.
explanation.walkthrough: TOUCH FASTER is rearranged with N set inside it to give COUNTERSHAFT.
explanation.definitionFit: A countershaft is an intermediate shaft in a machine that takes drive from the main shaft and passes it on.

clue.text: Scotch liquor king left off enjoying as of old

indicators.note: something left off is omitted, so the royal piece is taken away from the longer word
flags an archaic sense of the word, which a solver needs in order to find it

blocks.note: taken as written; these letters are the ones removed
brook once meant to enjoy or have the use of, so enjoying in that old sense

explanation.surface: A Scottish drink from which the king abstained, as people enjoyed it in the old days.
explanation.walkthrough: BROOKING, an archaic word for enjoying, drops KING to leave BROO. Broo is Scots for broth or liquid; 'Scotch' here just means Scottish.
explanation.definitionFit: Broo is a Scots word for broth or the liquid something is cooked in, so a Scottish liquor in the cooking sense.

clue.text: Type of clover grown for forage and oil possibly

definitions.text: Type of clover grown for forage

indicators.note: possibly says the letters could form something else if rearranged

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A farmer's note on a clover crop that is grown both for animal feed and for oil.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole first part is the definition; 'and oil possibly' is the wordplay, though it reads like a second use of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Ladino is a large white clover variety grown as a forage crop for livestock.

clue.text: Bad news for apiaries left our bee damaged in nourishment

indicators.note: damaged things are knocked out of shape, so the letters are rearranged
in places the rearranged letters inside the word for nourishment

blocks.note: nourishment is food; it is split open to take the other letters
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written
the letter B is spelt bee

explanation.surface: A beekeeper laments that their bee's food supply has been spoilt, which is bad for hives.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Our bee' reads as the beekeeper's insect, but bee is just the letter B, rearranged with 'left' and 'our'.
explanation.definitionFit: Foulbrood is a bacterial disease that kills bee larvae, a serious threat to beekeepers and their hives.

clue.text: As to churning in stomach, not affected by the environment

indicators.note: churning stirs things up, so the letters are rearranged
in puts the rearranged letters inside the stomach word

blocks.note: the bible is the third stomach of a ruminant, also called the omasum; it is split open
the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A stomach that churns, yet stays unaffected by surroundings.
explanation.walkthrough: AS TO rearranged as OSTA goes into BIBLE. A cow's third stomach is called the bible because its folds look like pages.
explanation.definitionFit: Biostable describes something that resists biological breakdown and stays unchanged in its environment.

clue.text: Old umpires may end batting (or bowling) round start of shower

indicators.note: batting or bowling a ball sends it spinning about, so the letters are thrown into a new order
round means the shuffled letters go around the other piece
the start of a word is its first letter

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged
the first letter of shower

explanation.surface: A cricket match may be cut short when a shower starts mid-innings, as old umpires knew.
explanation.walkthrough: MAY END rearranged gives DAYMEN, which wraps round S to make DAYSMEN. The cricket words in brackets are the anagram signal, not part of the picture.
explanation.definitionFit: A daysman is an archaic word for an arbiter or umpire who settles a dispute on an appointed day.

clue.text: Measure no longer used in French river after time

indicators.note: after puts the river second, behind the single letter for time

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time
the Oise is a river in northern France that joins the Seine

explanation.surface: An obsolete unit of measurement found on a French river after a certain period.
explanation.walkthrough: T plus OISE gives TOISE.
explanation.definitionFit: A toise was an old French unit of length, about two metres, now obsolete.

clue.text: Sunday lunch? It may include greens

blocks.note: first meaning: the roast meat traditionally eaten for the British Sunday dinner
second meaning: greens is slang for low-grade cannabis, which can be rolled into a cigarette

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests the green vegetables served beside the roast, but 'greens' is drug slang for poor-quality cannabis, rolled in a joint.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is both a roast cut of meat served at a Sunday meal and a hand-rolled cannabis cigarette.

clue.text: Being a renegade always restricts job with bank

indicators.note: to restrict something is to confine it, so the word for always encloses the rest

blocks.note: ay (or aye) is an old and poetic word for always
a post is a position or job
an as (plural asar) is a glacial ridge or bank, also called an esker

explanation.surface: A defector always confines themself to a job at a bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bank' suggests money, but it is the rare geological sense: an as is a glacial ridge, more often called an esker.
explanation.definitionFit: Apostasy is the abandonment of one's faith or party, the state of being a renegade or turncoat.

clue.text: What makes one's dog bark when old and saintly?

indicators.note: flags an archaic form, so the word for bark must be an obsolete spelling

blocks.note: a dog that is one's own is one's pet
rine is an obsolete form of rind, the bark of a tree

explanation.surface: A riddle about what sets a dog barking in old age, and a saintly dog at that.
explanation.walkthrough: PET plus RINE gives PETRINE. 'Bark' suggests a dog's noise but is tree bark.
explanation.definitionFit: Petrine means relating to Saint Peter, so it is saintly in the sense of belonging to that apostle.

clue.text: Front of saloon with ageing flickering indicators

indicators.note: the front of a word is its first letter
flickering lights jump about, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the first letter of saloon
the letters of ageing, rearranged

explanation.surface: An old bar whose neon signs flicker at the front.
explanation.walkthrough: S plus a rearranged AGEING gives SIGNAGE.
explanation.definitionFit: Signage is the collective noun for signs, which are things that point the way or indicate.

clue.text: Piston rising and falling – it limits erosion

indicators.note: rising in a down entry means read upwards, so the first copy is backwards
falling in a down entry means read downwards, so the second copy follows as written

blocks.note: a ram is a piston, as in a hydraulic ram; this copy is read upwards
the same word used again, read downwards

explanation.surface: A piston moving up and down in an engine designed to prevent erosion.
explanation.walkthrough: One word for piston serves twice: up the grid it reads MAR, then down it reads RAM.
explanation.definitionFit: Marram is a coarse grass planted on sand dunes, whose roots bind the sand and check erosion by the wind.

clue.text: Drained Stour about to worry eel fisher

indicators.note: something drained is emptied, so only the outer letters of the river name are kept
about means going around, so the kept letters surround the word for worry

blocks.note: the Stour, an English river, emptied of its inside letters
to niggle is to worry or nag

explanation.surface: Someone fishing for eels in the river Stour after it has been drained.
explanation.walkthrough: The Stour is the name of several English rivers; 'drained' empties it of its middle letters, leaving only its ends.
explanation.definitionFit: To sniggle is to fish for eels by poking a baited hook into their holes, so a sniggler is an eel fisher.

clue.text: Cierge lit? to light one's way up these?

definitions.text: Cierge lit? to light one's way up these?
definitions.note: Griece is one flight of steps, and 'these' refers to the steps that make it up

indicators.note: lit means drunk, and a drunken word staggers into a new arrangement of its letters

blocks.note: a cierge is a large church candle; its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Is a church candle lit to light the way up these stairs?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines: a lit candle lights the way up a staircase. 'Lit' also says the candle's letters are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: A griece, or grece, is an old word for a flight of steps or stairs, which a candle would light.

clue.text: Perfumed oil, excessive when applied to Mary's middle

indicators.note: applying one thing to another joins them, so the two pieces are put side by side
the middle of a word is its central letters, here the two at its heart

blocks.note: OTT, over the top, means excessive
the two central letters of Mary

explanation.surface: Too much scented oil was put on a woman's waist.
explanation.walkthrough: OTT plus AR gives OTTAR. 'Mary's middle' looks like her body but is the centre of her name.
explanation.definitionFit: Ottar is a variant spelling of attar, a fragrant essential oil distilled from rose petals.

clue.text: Game birds, number not appearing in transport

indicators.note: not appearing means absent, so that letter is removed from the longer word

blocks.note: N is the abbreviation for number
to convey is to transport

explanation.surface: A flock of grouse that did not show up when transported.
explanation.walkthrough: CONVEY without N gives COVEY.
explanation.definitionFit: A covey is a small flock of game birds such as partridge or grouse.

clue.text: Is stuffing rubbish with minimum of sage?

definitions.note: Craps is the Scots verb crap, to stuff or cram, in the third person, so 'is stuffing' stands in for it

indicators.note: the minimum of a word is the least of it, a single letter from its front

blocks.note: slang for rubbish or nonsense
the opening letter of sage

explanation.surface: A cook asks whether a poultry stuffing is no good because it has too little sage.
explanation.walkthrough: CRAP plus S gives CRAPS, not the dice game here: crap is a Scots verb meaning to stuff, as in crappit heid, a stuffed haddock head.
explanation.definitionFit: In Scots, crap means to fill or cram, so someone who craps something is stuffing it.

clue.text: Bacteriologist exchanging parts of entrails

indicators.note: exchanging parts means the two sections of the word swap places

blocks.note: tripe is stomach lining, entrails eaten as food; its back two letters move to the front

explanation.surface: A lab scientist swaps around bits of animal guts.
explanation.walkthrough: This is not a free anagram: the word splits into two chunks that change places whole, each keeping its own letter order.
explanation.definitionFit: Julius Petri was the German bacteriologist who gave his name to the petri dish.

clue.text: Stole recipe forming new centre of lecture

indicators.note: a new centre means the letter at the middle is swapped for another

blocks.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe (Latin, take) on prescriptions
a formal speech or lecture; its middle letter T is replaced

explanation.surface: A speaker lifted a recipe and built a lecture around it.
explanation.walkthrough: R replaces the central T of ORATION to give ORARION. 'Stole' looks like a verb, but it is the vestment.
explanation.definitionFit: An orarion is the long narrow stole worn by a deacon in the Eastern Orthodox Church.

clue.text: Beat song with loud opening

indicators.note: an opening comes first, so the loud letter goes at the start

blocks.note: F is forte, the musical direction for loud
a lay is a song or ballad

explanation.surface: A rhythm for a song that begins loudly.
explanation.walkthrough: F plus LAY gives FLAY. 'Beat' suggests musical rhythm but is to thrash.
explanation.definitionFit: To flay is to whip or thrash severely, so beat in the sense of punish physically.

clue.text: Lentil meal a Levanter transported

indicators.note: something transported is carried off and rearranged, so the letters are reordered

blocks.note: the letters to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Lentil flour carried by a person from the eastern Mediterranean.
explanation.walkthrough: A Levanter is someone from the Levant, or a strong easterly wind there; both fit 'transported'.
explanation.definitionFit: Revalenta was a Victorian patent food made from ground lentils, sold as an invalid's meal.

clue.text: Organ begins with this Caprice for Angela

indicators.note: a caprice is a whim or a lively free-form piece, so the letters are rearranged at will

blocks.note: a name whose letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: An organist starts a recital with a capriccio written for someone called Angela.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Organ' suggests the instrument and 'Caprice' a musical piece, but the organ is a body part and the caprice reorders ANGELA.
explanation.definitionFit: An anlage is the primordial cell cluster in an embryo from which a body part or organ develops.

clue.text: National symbol maybe, runner losing lead

indicators.note: losing its lead means the first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a racer is one who runs in a race

explanation.surface: A national sporting hero, perhaps, as an athlete falls out of first place.
explanation.walkthrough: RACER loses its first letter. The maple leaf is Canada's national symbol, and Acer is the maple genus.
explanation.definitionFit: Acer is the botanical genus of maples, and the maple leaf is Canada's national emblem, hence 'maybe'.

clue.text: Suitable spot, lake, this writer's written about

indicators.note: written about means set around, so the setter's possessive encloses the lake abbreviation

blocks.note: to spot something is to see it
the setter speaking of what belongs to him
L is the map abbreviation for lake

explanation.surface: A writer describes a fitting place by a lake for his story.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spot' looks like a noun for a place, but it is the verb, to see; 'this writer' is the setter himself.
explanation.definitionFit: Seemly means proper or appropriate in conduct or appearance, so fitting or suitable.

clue.text: Sort of hollow marriage, retrograde? One's sure trapped in it

indicators.note: retrograde means moving backwards, so the word for marriage is read the other way
something trapped in another is held inside it

blocks.note: a tie is a bond or union, as marriage is
yep is an informal yes, said by someone who is sure

explanation.surface: A hollow marriage going backwards, with one partner insisting they are sure they are trapped.
explanation.walkthrough: TIE backwards is EIT, which holds YEP to make EYEPIT. 'Hollow marriage' is a false phrase: 'hollow' belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: An eye-pit is the eye socket, a hollow in the skull, so it is one particular kind of hollow.
